_comment: Paper verdicts page -- which reviewed papers' claims SAO actually tested on SA3/SAME, and what happened. THE-FINN owns the content (add a row whenever a paper is reviewed and something is decided/run/discovered). WINTERMUTE owns the page build (build_paper_verdicts.py -> paper_verdicts.html). Sections ordered so the load-bearing content (nulled negative results, partial, confirmed) comes first; 'untested -- reviewed only' is a short reference list at the end. Each entry: id, title, link (arXiv/ACL abs url or null), claim, explanation, caveats (omit if none). Untested-section entries carry only id/title/link/claim -- no explanation/caveats prose, to keep that list scannable.

sections.title: Nulled — negative results
sections.blurb: The paper's mechanism was actually built and run on SA3/SAME, and it did not work, or made no measurable difference. These are the most informative entries on this page for anyone deciding whether to port the same idea.

entries.title: LoL: Longer than Longer, Scaling Video Generation to Hour
entries.claim: In autoregressive long-video generation with KV-cache attention sinks, head-shared RoPE causes inter-head phase concentration ("sink-collapse") at rotary phase-coherence maxima; jittering each head's RoPE base frequency (θ̂_h = θ0(1+σθ·ε_h)) de-synchronizes heads and breaks the resulting loop attractor.
entries.explanation: SAO built rope_jitter.py (per-head RoPE base-frequency jitter, citing LoL directly in its docstring) and ran it on longform.py as the team's #1 recommended long-form-coherence fix. The result was null: loopiness metric moved 0.704→0.709 (baseline 0.6707), essentially no change, reported in profiles/wintermute.journal.md 2026-07-12 ("RoPE jitter is null-by-construction on longform.py") and corroborated in WORKLOG.md and AGENT_DIALOGUE.md (2026-07-15, Gemini report #2 assessment: "we ran rope_jitter and got a null on loopiness"). Code-level tracing found the reason: LoL's sink-collapse requires RoPE positions to extend beyond a native window so distant frames alias onto a clamped prefix, but SA3's longform.py resets positions to 0..W every window and fifo_infinite.py uses a fixed 0..256 buffer — the aliasing condition the jitter targets never arises in SA3's bidirectional-DiT windowed regeneration, unlike LoL's autoregressive KV-cache setting.
entries.caveats: Not treated as a closed case against LoL's mechanism itself — it's flagged as an open structural-analogy question (SA3 is bidirectional-window denoising, not autoregressive with attention sinks, so the pathology may simply not transfer) rather than a refutation of LoL's claim in its own (AR) setting. A follow-up diagnostic (E3, phase-alignment) was designed to determine whether the null means "LoL's pathology isn't ours" or "our null needs a re-look inside LoL's σθ∈[0.05,0.10] band" (docs/ai-research/validation-experiment-plan-2026-07-15.md) — as of the material reviewed, E3 is still queued, not yet executed.

entries.title: InfiniteAudio: Infinite-Length Audio Generation with Consistent Acoustic Attributes
entries.claim: A FIFO/'diagonal denoising' scheme (staggered per-frame noise levels, rolling the denoising window forward frame-by-frame) enables infinite-length generation with consistent acoustic attributes, avoiding the drift of naive autoregressive continuation.
entries.explanation: The team actually ported this method to SA3 (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-18: "Ported InfiniteAudio (arXiv:2506.03020) long-form / FIFO diagonal denoising to SA3"), requiring real model surgery since SA3's DiT only accepts a scalar-per-batch timestep and had to be monkeypatched to accept per-token (B,T) sigmas. When GPU-validated (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-21), the FIFO prototype 'cratered to ~0.03 at ~18s' on the drift/RMS metric, versus a competing sliding-window inpaint-continuation approach that stayed flat ([1.03, 0.95, 0.75, 0.83, 1.04]). The stated root cause: per-frame timesteps are out-of-distribution for a model only ever trained on a global scalar timestep — the method's core mechanism doesn't transfer to an architecture trained without per-frame noise conditioning.
entries.caveats: Not a rejection of the paper's method in its native setting (video-DiT models trained for per-frame noise) — the null is specifically "untrained/OOD on our checkpoint." The team explicitly kept the FIFO code as a future 'Approach C' engine, to be revisited after a targeted finetune that would let the model learn per-frame timestep conditioning, so this could flip to confirmed/partial post-finetune. As of the 2026-07-15 longform assessment, the per-token (B,T) timestep surgery is cited approvingly as already-built infra even though the diagonal-denoising sampling mode itself was the part that failed.

entries.title: Du et al. — gradient-cosine gating (gate aux losses by grad cosine ≥ 0, MTL task-gradient conflict)
entries.claim: Auxiliary losses in multi-task learning can be gated by the cosine similarity between their gradient and the main task's gradient, downweighting or skipping the update whenever the two gradients conflict.
entries.explanation: Cited, not independently fetched (no local PDF) — but this is a genuine tested-against-our-data comparison, not a bare citation. knowledge.md: "Their predictor MISCLASSIFIES our genre case as harmless — the gate can't see manifold-confinement harm (not gradient conflict)." The team checked whether this paper's published gating heuristic would have caught their own known-harmful case (the genre-consistency probe that actively hurt steering when used as an auxiliary loss target) and found it would not have: the harm there comes from confining the generative manifold, a failure mode gradient-cosine conflict is blind to.
entries.caveats: Framed, per the team's own house style, as "a gap their predictor doesn't cover" rather than a head-on refutation of the paper's method in its own (discriminative multi-task) setting.

sections.title: Partial
sections.blurb: Real experiments were run and something worked, but not the whole claim — a sub-claim held while another failed, the effect showed up on one axis but not another, or the tested version differed from the paper's exact proposal.

entries.title: Cautious Weight Decay (modded-nanogpt speedrun optimizer work)
entries.claim: Applying 'cautious' masking (only updating coordinates where the update and gradient sign agree) specifically to the weight-decay term of an optimizer improves training speed/quality without the pitfalls of masking the full update.
entries.explanation: The team ran a real cautious-optimizer A/B campaign on SA3/FusionOpt (2026-06-30 to 07-02) applying the original, broader Liang et al. 2024-style cautious masking to the FULL update — not the weight-decay-only variant this specific paper proposes — on top of a Muon/Newton-Schulz (NS5) orthogonalized optimizer path. It found a genuine, reproducible negative result: on orthogonalized paths the sign-agreement between update and raw gradient sits at keep_frac ~0.53 (barely above chance) flat across 54k steps, making cautious masking there 'a near-random ~50% sparsification' with no measured control-authority or trajectory-geometry benefit, and the standard 1/keep_frac rescale silently inflates update norm by ~1.37x, which NaN'd a rank-128 DoRA finetune (docs/findings-2026-07-02-perceptual-signal-night.md; docs/research-brief-2026-07-03-novelty-check.md). The team's own verified citation pass checked this finding against 2510.12402 and found the paper's scope is narrower (weight-decay-only caution) and does not report this failure mode: "Nobody reported our failure mechanism."
entries.caveats: The experiment does not directly test 2510.12402's actual proposal (restricting caution to weight decay) — it tests the more general/naive cautious-masking idea against an orthogonalized optimizer, and the paper's narrower design would plausibly sidestep the exact bug the team found, since weight decay itself isn't Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized. The paper functions here mainly as the closest published boundary-setter the team checked its real, negative finding against.

entries.title: TADA! Tuning Audio Diffusion Models through Activation Steering
entries.claim: Activation patching reveals a small cross-attention 'semantic bottleneck' (layers {12,13}/24 in Stable Audio Open) that causally controls nearly all high-level musical concepts, and steering methods work best when confined to those layers; weight-space (LoRA) sliders confined the same way get WORSE.
entries.explanation: The team built its own causal localizer (Axis-1, layer_patch_map.py) extending TADA's activation-patching protocol from cross-attention to all three module types, and ran it on SA3 medium-base (1728 patching cells; wintermute.journal.md 2026-07-10). Result: onset density, bass weight, brightness and noisiness all localize to LATE blocks (~16-23) via self-attention and feed-forward, with cross-attention impact scores at 0.00 at every layer — the opposite shape from TADA's cross-attn-{12,13} bottleneck. However, a separate correlational strand of the team's own work lands in TADA's own territory and agrees with it: a layer x feature ridge-R2 map (docs/layer-feature-map.md) shows rhythm/onset features are 'computed' mid-stack (beat R2 peaks at L11-14), and a held-out mood-classifier probe shows categorical mood concepts peak at L8-15 — squarely inside TADA's {12,13}.
entries.caveats: TADA's own localization was measured on Stable Audio Open (acoustics-only conv-VAE) using categorical concept pairs; SAO's causal test used SA3 (semantic SAME-VAE) with continuous acoustic attributes, so the two experiments are not a strict apples-to-apples replication even where they diverge. Net picture, in the team's own words: 'different question (acoustic realization vs categorical semantics), different answer' — not a clean confirmation or a clean refutation.

entries.title: Stable Audio 3 (technical report — our own model)
entries.claim: Reports SA3's own architecture and training recipe: three conditioning pathways, logit-normal timestep sampling truncated at t=0.075, length-dependent timestep shift, TrackType/AudioSparx prompt-prefix convention, Muon+AdamW optimizer split, layer-14 discriminator tap, etc.
entries.explanation: Several of the paper's own claims were checked against actual model/code behavior with mixed results. (1) TrackType prefix: the paper recommends a specific prefix at inference for quality; the team discovered this prefix was missing from every one of their own captions and eval prompts, and fixed it, then ran a controlled A/B across 5 prompt-style arms (WORKLOG.md 2026-07-06/07). (2) The t<0.075-untrained crispness mechanism: initially taken at face value, then CORRECTED on 2026-07-07 after reading the actual sampler code — the truncation reshapes density, not support, so the finishing regime is thinly-trained rather than literally untrained; the crispness-late mechanism 'survives in weakened form'. (3) The layer-14 discriminator-tap hint and the init_noise_level sweet spots (0.4-0.5 timbre, 0.6 style) were both corroborated by independently-run experiments. (4) LoRA portability from base to post-trained checkpoint, stated by the repo guides, is explicitly flagged as untested.
entries.caveats: As the paper describing the team's own model, this is 'checking our own spec against our own code and outputs' rather than testing an external claim; several sub-items are confirmed while one (the untrained-region claim) required a real correction, hence 'partial' rather than a clean 'confirmed'.

entries.title: SHIFT: Steering Hidden Intermediates in Flow Transformers
entries.claim: A single, time-independent (temporally invariant) activation-steering vector, dual-injected into the text-encoder pooled embedding and DiT text-token activations with dynamic cosine-similarity-based per-step scaling, gives training-free concept removal/stylization control in MM-DiT flow models.
entries.explanation: The paper's headline empirical claim — that steering directions are stable across diffusion timesteps/noise levels rather than needing per-step vectors — was directly tested and replicated on SA3: diff-in-means mood-concept directions showed cross-sigma direction-cosine stability of .93-.99 across the DiT's mid-stack layers, explicitly logged as SHIFT's finding replicating on the team's own audio model (profiles/continuity.journal.md 2026-07-11). A same-day closed-loop steering render then verified training-free directional control works on SA3 (mt_dark 0.018→0.341 at alpha=+2), though that test used single-direction injection into the conditional CFG branch, not SHIFT's dual injection or its dynamic per-step scaling.
entries.caveats: Only the temporal-invariance sub-claim was tested and confirmed; the actual SHIFT mechanism (dual-hook injection with concept-presence-gated dynamic scaling, aimed at concept erasure specifically) has not been built or tested on SA3 — it remains an open item, with hook (c) flagged as needing re-derivation for SA3's separate cross-attention, unlike SHIFT's joint-attention MM-DiT target.

entries.title: SaFa: Latent Swap Joint Diffusion for 2D Long-Form Latent Generation (ICCV 2025)
entries.claim: Replacing latent averaging/blending at generation-window overlaps with bidirectional latent swaps (joint denoising reconciling both windows) produces cleaner, higher-fidelity long-form joins than naive overlap-averaging.
entries.explanation: The team built a direct A/B comparing a frame-interleave latent-SWAP join against their existing slerp/averaging bridge for SA3 longform window stitching, targeting the RMS/HF-variance collapse mechanism SaFa's paper identifies. Result (2026-07-13): swap join holds seam HF-variance at 1.159x versus slerp's suppression to 0.818x, with RMS ratio ~1.0 in both arms — confirming the paper's mechanism (averaging specifically suppresses high-frequency variance at seams, not overall energy). A same-day co-score found the swap join's loopiness metric identical to slerp's, 0.680 = 0.680 — the join method does not touch the loop-repetition failure mode at all. Team verdict, stated explicitly: "SaFa's win is REAL but NARROW" — confirmed on the seam-HF-variance axis, null on the loopiness axis.
entries.caveats: This tested only SaFa's core swap-join operator via a join-level frame-interleave approximation, not the paper's full per-step joint-diffusion sequential renderer — an upgrade to the exact algorithm is a pending pool item. The paper's second operator (Reference-Guided Latent Swap, for cross-window timbre/acoustic drift) was separately identified as never having been ported, so that half of SaFa remains genuinely untested on SA3.

entries.title: Physics-aware auxiliary losses (states a redundancy condition near-verbatim, discriminative GNN setting)
entries.claim: In a discriminative GNN setting, a redundant auxiliary loss (one carrying no information beyond the main task) is neutral rather than harmful.
entries.explanation: Cited, not independently fetched (no local PDF), but this is a genuine comparison against the team's own tested finding. knowledge.md: "Finds redundant aux NEUTRAL, not harmful — our generative-manifold degradation goes beyond it." The team's own finding (a redundant auxiliary loss — the genre-consistency probe — is actively harmful in their generative-manifold setting) goes further than / partially contradicts this paper's finding in a different problem setting.
entries.caveats: Not a like-for-like replication (discriminative GNN vs. generative rectified-flow manifold) — worded here as 'partial / nulled-in-a-different-domain' rather than a direct refutation.

sections.title: Confirmed
sections.blurb: The paper's claim was tested (directly, or via a deliberately cheaper/adapted version of its method) and held up on SA3/SAME's own evidence.

entries.title: Discovering and Steering Interpretable Concepts in Large Generative Music Models
entries.claim: Sparse autoencoders trained on a music generator's residual stream discover human-interpretable concepts, and simple activation-addition (adding a decoder direction) steers generation toward those concepts for a meaningful (15-35%) fraction of features, audibly to listeners.
entries.explanation: The team explicitly skipped the SAE-training step (citing AxBench's finding that supervised directions beat SAE features for LLMs) and instead ran the cheaper, paper-inspired experiment directly: diff-in-means concept directions computed from labeled MIR/mood features on SA3's own DiT activation dumps, injected at mid/late blocks via conditional-branch-only activation addition. Phase 3 landed the same day: mt_dark steered Essentia dark score 0.018 → 0.341 at alpha=+2 (19x, zero training); mt_uplifting steered only in the negative direction; mt_relaxing was dead — summarized in-journal as '1 clean + 1 partial of 3 moods ~ the MusicGen paper's 15-35% steerable fraction; "select the right features" holds' (profiles/continuity.journal.md, 2026-07-11). Cross-sigma direction stability of .93-.99 was also measured in the same run.
entries.caveats: This is a training-free activation-addition experiment on SA3's DiT residual stream using supervised (diff-in-means) directions rather than SAE-discovered ones, so it tests the paper's steering claim and steerable-fraction finding, not its SAE-discovery pipeline itself; the paper's own abstract file already anticipated this as the 'cheap follow-up' before it was run.

entries.title: SAME: A Semantically-Aligned Music Autoencoder (our own latent space)
entries.claim: SAME's soft-normalization latent bottleneck (not a VAE) has semantics trained in via a joint flow-matching alignment loss, linear chroma/ILD regressors, and contrastive text alignment, producing a decode-robust, linearly-decodable, text-aligned latent space — and the paper cautions this differs architecturally from Stable Audio Open's acoustics-only conv-VAE.
entries.explanation: Two of SAME's specific claims were tested and held up. First, the trained-in linear decodability claim: the team's own layer x feature ridge-R2 map found spectral flux/flatness/skewness already near-ceiling R2 (0.86-0.94) at layer 0 of the DiT — direct evidence these regressor-trained features are linear by construction, not emergent. Second, the paper's own explicit caution that SA3's semantic bottleneck 'may sit elsewhere' than TADA's Stable-Audio-Open-derived {12,13} because SAME's semantics are trained in differently — this caution was directly acted on and tested via the Axis-1 causal localizer, which found SA3's acoustic-attribute localization is indeed NOT at cross-attn {12,13} but at late self-attn/FF blocks, vindicating the paper's caution against blind transplantation.
entries.caveats: The localizer test that vindicates SAME's caution is the same experiment cited under the TADA! entry above (see Partial); it confirms the caution (don't assume the same bottleneck location) rather than pinning down where SAME's own semantic bottleneck specifically lives — mood/concept probes suggest mid-stack layers 8-15 for categorical concepts, while causal acoustic-attribute patching lands late at 16-23, so 'elsewhere' is itself feature-dependent.

entries.title: DirectAudioEdit: Inversion-Free Text-Guided Audio Editing via Diffusion Prediction Contrast
entries.claim: Training-free, inversion-free text-guided audio editing on DDPM-style backbones requires shared-noise re-noising plus one-step reverse-dynamics contrast (not raw prediction contrast), with a dynamic increasing target-CFG schedule, because diffusion's SDE paths are curved.
entries.explanation: SAO did not build DirectAudioEdit's DDPM-specific machinery (its mel+vocoder backbone fails the hard filters), but the team ran the lineage this paper's own reasoning points to for SA3: FlowEdit's raw source/target velocity-difference contrast, ported to SA3's rectified-flow latents (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-18, sa3_flowsep.py, working and 'robust to high cfg' with concrete separation numbers against a true-inversion baseline). The 2026-07-06 sourcebook revisit explicitly cross-references DirectAudioEdit against the FlowEdit chapter entry as 'independent corroboration that RF's straight paths don't need DirectAudioEdit's heavier re-noising machinery' — the already-run FlowEdit experiment plus this paper's own stated rationale jointly confirm the simpler-contrast approach was the right call for SA3.
entries.caveats: This is confirmation-by-comparison, not a literal test of DirectAudioEdit's own method on SA3 (its DDPM machinery was never implemented or run against ours) — the paper itself was never executed; what's confirmed is the choice to keep developing FlowEdit's simpler contrast instead of building DirectAudioEdit's heavier variant.

entries.title: Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval Improves Sample and Distribution Quality in Diffusion Models (Kynkäänniemi et al., NeurIPS 2024)
entries.claim: Classifier-free guidance should only be applied within a limited interval of noise levels (sigma range), not across the whole sampling trajectory, to improve sample/distribution quality; CFG applied broadly is most mode-collapsing in the mid-noise band.
entries.explanation: SA3's own DiT already implements this natively as sigma-gated limited-interval guidance (dit.py:479), and the team's own explorer UI iteration (2026-07-08) surfaced it directly: a sigma-schedule chart with a range-slider-driven cfg_interval control, the chat announcement of that UI work described it as SA3's 'native limited-interval guidance (DiT sigma-gated, Kynkaanniemi 2024)' finally surfaced for hands-on use (AGENT_DIALOGUE.md, 2026-07-08). Separately, and independently corroborating the paper's own headline claim, WINTERMUTE's melodic_movement_ladder measurement found a real U-shaped mode-collapse in a2a chroma-flux/pc-transition metrics that bottoms exactly in the mid-noise band (nl .40-.55, -20% vs source) and recovers/overshoots outside it — matched explicitly to 'Kynkaanniemi NeurIPS-24 (CFG most mode-collapsing in the mid band)' (profiles/wintermute.journal.md, 2026-07-08).
entries.caveats: The mechanism is built into SA3's own inherited DiT architecture rather than something the team implemented from the paper themselves — the team's contribution was surfacing/exposing an existing native control and independently measuring a real-data pattern consistent with the paper's claim, not re-deriving or ablating the guidance-interval method itself. A follow-up controlled A/B (interval-limited CFG vs. chroma-guided steering in the mid-band) was proposed but not yet reported as run.

entries.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs, Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
entries.claim: On a systematic LLM steering benchmark, simple supervised baselines (e.g. difference-in-means / linear probes) outperform Sparse Autoencoder (SAE)-based steering methods.
entries.explanation: The team explicitly invoked AxBench's finding as the reason to skip building an SAE steering pipeline for SA3 and go straight to a supervised diff-in-means approach (AGENT_DIALOGUE.md, 2026-07-11). They then built and ran exactly that simple baseline on SA3's DiT activations and it worked well: mood concepts separated cleanly at L8-15 with split-half held-out AUCs of .69-.93, and Phase 3 injection produced real, audible, closed-loop-verified steering on SA3 (mt_dark 0.018→0.341 at alpha=+2). No SAE arm was ever separately trained and benchmarked head-to-head on SA3, so this is confirmation-by-application (the simple baseline AxBench recommends was sufficient and successful) rather than a controlled SAE-vs-diff-in-means bake-off on the team's own stack.
entries.caveats: Not a true head-to-head replication — the team never built a comparison SAE steering baseline on SA3 to test against; they took AxBench's finding on faith and it paid off. A 2026-07-13 summary listing 'SAE-vs-supervised' among the week's research-verification wins somewhat overstates the rigor of what was actually a one-arm application, not a comparison.

sections.title: Independent convergence
sections.blurb: The team built the same mechanism the paper describes before finding (or independently of finding) the paper itself, typically discovered afterward during a deliberate novelty/prior-art check.

entries.title: ControlNet++: Improving Conditional Controls with Efficient Consistency Feedback
entries.claim: Controllable diffusion adapters can be trained with a cycle-consistency loss: noise the input, take a one-step denoised estimate, score it with a frozen off-the-shelf discriminative 'meter', and back-propagate a t-gated (low-noise-only) consistency loss into the adapter, instead of relying only on the base diffusion loss.
entries.explanation: The team built 'FusionCC' — a loss that decodes a one-step denoised latent estimate (rf_z0_hat), scores it with a frozen probe, and back-propagates a timestep-gated consistency loss into an adapter — and only discovered ControlNet++ afterward during a deliberate novelty/prior-art check. The team's own verified citation pass states it plainly: "mechanism-identical to FusionCC — the prior-art call stands, no wiggle room" (docs/research-brief-2026-07-03-novelty-check.md; AGENT_DIALOGUE.md 2026-07-03). FusionCC's onset-density variant trained 2026-07-02 and posted the campaign's first statistically significant win (corr .584→.880 at gain 2, bootstrap CI excludes zero; re-confirmed on a corrected onset meter). A companion run applying the same recipe to a genre-consistency probe (a global, RF-visible property) actively hurt steering (0.92→0.65), giving the team a boundary condition — 'the meter must carry information the training loss doesn't already have' — that the ControlNet++ line does not state.
entries.caveats: The paper's own t-gate scales window width with how 'global' the metered property is (edges 200 vs depth 400 out of 1000); the team's boundary condition (blind-vs-redundant) and the genre negative control are noted internally as the unpublished addition on top of the reinvented mechanism, not a criticism of the paper.

entries.title: InnerControl ("Heeding the Inner Voice"): all-timestep alignment via t-conditioned probes on intermediate diffusion features
entries.claim: Cycle-consistency control losses that only work on clean (low-noise) latent estimates fail when extended naively to noisy/early timesteps (alignment improves but quality craters); the fix is to train lightweight t-conditioned probes directly on noisy intermediate features so the alignment signal can be applied across nearly the whole denoising trajectory.
entries.explanation: SA3's LatCH ('Latent-Control Heads') already implement t-conditioned probes via a t_injection mechanism, built and validated in the CPU LatCH-guidance eval path from 2026-06-28/06-29 (docs/latch.md) — roughly a week before the team's deep-read of InnerControl on 2026-07-03. After the deep-read, the team explicitly designed a direct application — 'FusionCC v1.3': replacing FusionCC's clean-z0 probe with a t-conditioned meter on noised latents for all-timestep supervision (WORKLOG.md 2026-07-03). That extension was deliberately deferred, not run: "designed, deliberately deferred, not lost…parked because the plain-CC scope condition needed validating first" (docs/onset-density-control-narrative.md).
entries.caveats: Two distinct things map onto this paper: (1) LatCH's pre-existing t-conditioned probes are a genuine independent convergence on the paper's core mechanism, predating the paper's discovery; (2) the direct, paper-inspired extension of FusionCC to an all-timestep t-conditioned probe (FusionCC v1.3) was designed but never trained — a declined/deferred experiment with a stated reason, not a run one.

entries.title: Optimizer-Induced Low-Dimensional Drift and Transverse Dynamics ("Backbone" trajectory-PCA)
entries.claim: 60-80% of optimizer displacement during training concentrates in a low-dimensional subspace under uncentered PCA, attributed to optimizer-induced structure.
entries.explanation: The team ran its own checkpoint-trajectory PCA on a ~120M-parameter adapter fine-tune (10 checkpoints, Gram-trick PCA validated against a random-walk null) during the 2026-07-01/02 'perceptual-signal night' and found top-2 explained variance 0.969 vs 0.776 for the null, with 88% of weight motion in PC1 and a PC2 arc that turns over near epoch 5 — coinciding with the checkpoint-averaging centroid and Kim's independent audition sweet spot. The 2602.23696 paper was only surfaced afterward, during a 2026-07-03 novelty/citation check, as the nearest piece of prior art — the team had not read it before running its own PCA. On comparison the two findings differ in kind, not just degree: 2602.23696 uses uncentered PCA on raw displacement (60-80%); the team's is centered PCA on variance (88%, a stronger planarity statement) plus a PC2-turnover signal functioning as a loss-blind early-stopping proxy, which the paper does not report.
entries.caveats: This is prior-art discovered after independent derivation, not a test of the paper's specific claim — the team did not re-run an uncentered-PCA analysis to check whether the paper's own 60-80% figure holds on their stack; the comparison is at the level of method and interpretation, not a replication.

entries.title: Audio-to-Audio via Diffusion Warm Initialization
entries.claim: SDEdit-style warm-start diffusion has an empirically locatable skip-fraction sweet spot (found via a pitch-Jaccard-Distance + FAD metric sweep on Stable Audio Open), and re-adding noise to the guide (lambda=1) is usually unnecessary/can hurt versus treating the guide as already on the intermediate marginal (lambda=0).
entries.explanation: SAO's Longform feature already ships the identical mechanism — a whole-segment SDEdit re-anchor (SDEditReanchor in stable_audio_3/inference/longform.py) — and it was built and merged on 2026-06-19/2026-06-21, contemporaneous with or predating this paper's public posting; the team built the SDEdit-re-anchor idea on their own rather than adopting it from this paper. The sourcebook's 2026-07-06 revisit explicitly notes 'the mechanism is precisely Longform's already-shipped SDEdit re-anchor… No new capability here' and flags the paper's lambda=0-vs-1 finding as 'a mild confirmation of standard SDEdit practice, not a new finding for anyone who has already implemented and shipped this mechanism.'
entries.caveats: The paper's proposed JD+FAD metric-sweep tuning-harness pattern was explicitly noted as possibly useful ('worth a line…if re-anchor timestep selection is ever revisited') but a search of the logs turns up no evidence it was actually adopted — Longform's re-anchor timestep remains hand-set, not metric-swept, as far as the record shows.

entries.title: Low-Resource Guidance for Controllable Latent Audio Diffusion ("LatCH" source paper)
entries.claim: Training-free guidance (TFG-style rho/mu variance/mean guidance, gamma noise-convolution, n_iter mean-guidance iterations) using small MIR-feature prediction heads on noisy latents can steer a frozen latent audio diffusion model toward requested control targets without retraining the base model.
entries.explanation: The team's own LatCH guidance-head infrastructure (docs/latch.md; latch_guided.py with exactly the paper's rho/mu/gamma/n_iter TFG parameterization) was built and iterated starting no later than 2026-05-31, and was ported to SA3 through June-July 2026 (onset head steering 2026-06-23, chroma/beat/hardness heads through 07-10). The team only recognized this exact paper as the method's source on 2026-07-15, via a cross-check: "LatCH 2603.04366 is REAL, ICASSP 2026, authors = THE STABLE AUDIO TEAM…our latch infra implements it per LATCH_README." A follow-up read of the full paper confirmed the TFG design space (rho/mu, gamma, n_iter, selective step windows, multi-guide weighting) is fully ported and working on SA3.
entries.caveats: This is a genuine independent-convergence case, not a validated port: the team built the mechanism first and discovered the paper as prior art afterward. Three paper components were explicitly identified as NOT yet ported/tested: LatCH-B (backwards-simulated/rollout-trained heads), the sparsity-aware loss for high-dimensional sparse targets, and N_recur time-travel recurrence — these remain untested future work, not confirmed-working replications.

entries.title: TAC-GAN (AC-GAN outputs confined by frozen auxiliary classifier decision boundaries)
entries.claim: An auxiliary discriminative classifier's decision boundary can be used to confine/steer generative outputs, without redundancy conditioning.
entries.explanation: Cited, not independently fetched (no local PDF). knowledge.md: "the HARM mechanism of our boundary condition, formalized — but with no redundancy conditioning." Independent-convergence-flavored: the team found this mechanism themselves (the manifold-confinement harm behind their genre-consistency negative result); this paper names/formalizes half of it, and was surfaced as prior art rather than a source the team built from.
entries.caveats: No PDF fetched; the citation is used only for the boundary-condition writeup, not as a tested-against comparison in its own right.

sections.title: Declined to test
sections.blurb: A reasoned, documented decision not to run the paper's method, with a stated reason and (where applicable) a standing condition that would reopen the question.

entries.title: Entropy as a Structural Prior: How a Log-Barrier on DiT Belief Space Drives Musical Diversity and Development
entries.claim: A parameter-free per-sample loss-reweighting scheme (the 'Eisbach log-barrier', derived from a DiT output's own temporal-energy entropy) fights mode collapse in DoRA fine-tunes of Stable Audio 3 Medium by upweighting gradient for structurally dynamic samples and damping it for flat/loop-like ones.
entries.explanation: This is a documented, reasoned decision, not neglect. WINTERMUTE flagged the paper hard for scrutiny in a DM to THE-FINN (2026-07-06 exchange), citing single-seed/single-prompt evidence, purely qualitative spectrogram/PCA reads, self-deferred validating ablations, 6-of-14 'Anonymous' unverifiable citations, and DDPM/epsilon-prediction language mismatched to SA3's rectified-flow objective. CONTINUITY's reply states the verdict explicitly: "NO dedicated rerun — the tells you list…put it below the credibility bar the TADA incident taught us to enforce; GPU hours belong to planned work." The standing disposition is a conditional rider: if an actual future SAO run shows genuine mode collapse, the entropy-reweighting idea can be added as a ~10-line addition to that already-planned run, tested on SAO's own evidence rather than the paper's claims.
entries.caveats: knowledge.md's row for this paper is kept explicitly marked 'speculative' per this same exchange. As of the sources reviewed, no SAO run has yet exhibited the kind of mode collapse that would trigger the conditional rerun, so the rider has not been exercised.

sections.title: Untested — reviewed only
sections.blurb: Reviewed for landscape awareness, novelty-checking, or the literature shelf, but no experiment was run against SA3/SAME, and (unlike the section above) no reasoned decision to skip was recorded either — these are open, not closed.

entries.title: Live Music Diffusion Models (LMDM) / ARC-Forcing
entries.claim: A routing+attention-mask trick makes an offline block-outpainting rectified-flow music model KV-cacheable for low-latency streaming, and ARC-Forcing (an RL-free adversarial rollout-distillation objective) fixes the gradual quality drift that appears over long autoregressive rollouts. Status: greenlit as a build task, dataset builder and sbatch scaffolding exist, but the ARC rollout/train pipeline itself had not been submitted or completed as of the material reviewed (2026-07-17) — could tip to confirmed/nulled/partial once run.

entries.title: Diffusion Domain Expansion (DDE)
entries.claim: A small trained ViT coordinator (with RoPE positional encoding for length generalization) reconciles overlapping patches' predicted-clean (z0-hat) denoiser outputs, beating naive overlap-averaging for extending a frozen diffusion model beyond its trained length. Fails SA3's hard filters (raw-waveform UNet1d, DDPM/EDM not rectified flow); filed as a future ablation, not built or benchmarked against Longform's crossfade.

entries.title: DEMON (Diffusion Engine for Musical Orchestrated Noise)
entries.claim: A StreamDiffusion-style ring-buffer scheduler with per-slot heterogeneous denoise schedules and windowed VAE decode turns ACE-Step 1.5 into a live-playable instrument running at 12+ generations/sec. Systems/infra reference, not a control method; no ring-buffer or windowed-decode prototype ever built for SA3/SAME.

entries.title: UNISON — depth-matched text injection
entries.claim: Projecting different layers of a frozen instruction-LLM text encoder into depth-matched blocks of a flow-matching MM-DiT beats broadcasting a single penultimate-layer embedding to every block. Fails SA3's hard filters as shipped (MMAudio mel-spectrogram VAE); its Table 8 ablation is cited as a counter-example against a line in the team's own book chapter, but that's scored on UNISON's own backbone, not SA3 — no SA3 ablation run.

entries.title: Score-Control for Hallucination Reduction in Diffusion Models
entries.claim: Penalizing the score field's Jacobian norm (cheaply approximated via an I-DDPM variance-learning head) reduces off-manifold 'hallucination' probability mass in diffusion models while maintaining sample quality. Reviewed for prior-art awareness only; the tractable-Jacobian trick has no analog in SA3's rectified-flow velocity field and the paper is pixel/image-only — no rectified-flow analog ever derived or tried.

entries.title: SegTune: Structured and Fine-Grained Control for Song Generation
entries.claim: Hierarchical global+segment text conditioning, channel-concatenated per time-window rather than linearly mixed, improves song-generation control; the paper's own ablation shows concatenation beats linear-mix fusion. Lyrics/vocal song generation is out of SA3's scope; the concat-vs-linear-mix finding is cited as literature support for an existing design choice, not rerun on SAO's own conditioning stack.

entries.title: UAT: Unified Audio-Text Diffusion for Audio Generation, Editing, and Captioning
entries.claim: A dual-stream DiT where a text-token stream is actively co-updated (not just frozen cross-attention) alongside the audio latent stream lets one backbone perform generation, SDEdit-style editing, and masked-discrete-diffusion captioning. Fails SA3's filters (cosine/EDM schedule, weaker backbone by the paper's own ablation); no captioning/understanding thread exists on SAO for this to attach to.

entries.title: Unified Audio Generation and Editing via Joint Condition Modeling and Progressive Training (AudioWeave)
entries.claim: A single DiT can do TTA plus six instruction-editing tasks by concatenating reference-audio latents as context tokens (with factorized global/local RoPE) rather than channel-expansion, trained with a staged base-then-mix curriculum that beats naive joint training. Two portable ideas banked as reusable, but neither tried against SA3's own conditioning stack.

entries.title: Hybrid Diffusion Transformer for Instruction-Guided Audio Editing via Rectified Flow
entries.claim: A two-stage coarse-to-fine mel-domain DiT, trained with a rectified-flow objective and channel-concat source conditioning, achieves fast, small (78.6M param) instruction-guided audio editing when trained on a procedurally synthesized mix-two-clips add/remove/replace dataset. Architecturally hard-filtered out; the synthetic-data recipe is banked as an idea, not executed.

entries.title: STAR-VAE: Structured Topology-Aware Regularization for Audio Reconstruction and Generation
entries.claim: A channel-wise 'Gamma-Growth' power-law KL penalty forces low-index VAE latent channels to store structure and high-index channels to store texture, beating Stable Audio Open's own VAE on matched-rate reconstruction. SAME is treated as a frozen shipped component and hasn't been revisited at all for this comparison — not a reasoned decline, just not yet reached.

entries.title: SwiftAudio: Data-Efficient Caption-Only Distillation for One-Step Text-to-Audio Diffusion-based Generation
entries.claim: A DDPM mel-spectrogram text-to-audio teacher can be distilled to a one-step student using caption-only Variational Score Distillation, and an L1 temporal-TV latent regularizer measurably improves FAD/IS over no regularization or L2. SAO's own few-step distillation path solves the same top-level problem separately; the TV-on-z0_hat idea itself was never tried.

entries.title: General and Efficient Steering of Unconditional Diffusion
entries.claim: No local abstract file or knowledge.md row exists; presumed core claim per the title is a general, efficient method for steering an unconditional diffusion model's outputs post-hoc. Zero engagement found anywhere in the team's records — possibly worth double-checking against 2602.11910 (TADA!) for an arXiv-ID transcription slip, since all the team's actual steering work traces to that paper instead.

entries.title: STAS: Steering Video Diffusion Transformers with Massive Activations
entries.claim: Steering only at structurally-significant 'massive activation' tokens in a video DiT gives more effective, less disruptive activation steering than steering uniformly across all tokens. Appears once, as a literature-review analogy for possible beat-transient/measure-boundary-locked steering; no SA3 experiment, code, or eval references it.

entries.title: SteeringDiffusion: A Bottlenecked Activation Control Interface for Diffusion Models
entries.claim: Projecting a prompt-conditioned latent code through a FiLM/AdaGN-style bottleneck (frozen backbone, no per-layer rank matrices) gives a continuous, monotonic, runtime-adjustable style-control surface that outperforms LoRA at comparable content preservation. Appears only as a literature citation in a research report; no SA3 code, experiment, or eval engages it.

entries.title: UniSteer: Text-Guided Flow Matching in Activation Space for LLM Steering
entries.claim: A flow-matching model can be trained in an LLM's activation space to steer generations toward text-described attributes, generalizing beyond single fixed steering directions. No abstract file exists and no mention appears anywhere in the team's logs; reviewed for the literature shelf but never engaged, even as a cross-domain reference.

entries.title: Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering for Symbolic Music
entries.claim: Activation steering can disentangle and control musical attributes (e.g. style, texture) in a symbolic (MIDI) generative model's latent/activation space. The team's actual MIDI work (musicological transcription/analysis) never cites or engages this paper — unrelated methods despite overlapping domain.

entries.title: SongBloom: Coherent Song Generation via Interleaved AR Sketching and Diffusion Refinement
entries.claim: Coherent full-song generation via an interleaved cascade: a low-rate autoregressive 'sketch' pass establishes long-range song structure, followed by diffusion refinement to full-rate audio. A live candidate in the team's structure-prior roadmap, not a dead idea — not yet implemented, trained, or benchmarked against SA3's existing long-form pipeline.

entries.title: Similarity-Guided Diffusion for Long-Gap Music Inpainting (SimDPS)
entries.claim: Uses similarity-guided diffusion posterior sampling to bridge long gaps in music inpainting, guiding generation toward segments similar to the surrounding context. On the reading list for bridges/transitions since 2026-07-08; not yet read in depth or tested, and not among the items given a stated skip-reason.

entries.title: TC-LoRA: Temporally Modulated Conditional LoRA for Adaptive Diffusion Control
entries.claim: A hypernetwork generates LoRA weights on-the-fly, conditioned jointly on the diffusion timestep and an external control signal, so the effective adapter functionally shifts as generation proceeds from coarse layout to fine detail. Discussed only in a literature-survey doc as a possible future combination with steering vectors; all of SAO's actual LoRA/DoRA work is static-rank, no timestep-hypernetwork mechanism built or tested.

entries.title: DiffRhythm 2: Efficient and High Fidelity Song Generation via Block Flow Matching
entries.claim: A semi-autoregressive block-causal flow-matching scheme for song generation, combined with a 'stochastic-block REPA' auxiliary loss that aligns a mid-depth DiT hidden state to a frozen MuQ music-SSL teacher to speed convergence. Deferred as the 'LUMI-scale' native long-form answer; no REPA auxiliary loss, block-causal mask, or MuQ-teacher alignment implemented or run against SA3/SAME.

entries.title: UltraViCo: Breaking Extrapolation Limits in Video Diffusion Transformers
entries.claim: Extending video-DiT generation past its trained context window causes out-of-distribution tokens to disperse attention into periodic harmonic patterns, producing first blur/static degradation then cyclic repetition; the paper proposes attention-decay for out-of-window tokens as a plug-and-play fix. Folded into the team's theoretical mechanism-map for SA3's loop-attractor problem as a 'secondary' explanation, but its specific attention-decay fix (distinct from the RoPE-jitter idea that was actually tried and nulled, see LoL above) has never itself been built or tested.

entries.title: Timestep-Aware Data Augmentation for Diffusion Models (anonymous ICLR2024 submission — NOT the activation-steering "TADA!" paper, arXiv 2602.11910, despite the identical acronym)
entries.claim: Schedules/scales data-augmentation strength by diffusion timestep during training. Picked up only as a byproduct of chasing down an acronym mix-up (two unrelated papers share the 'TADA' acronym); kept on the shelf as thematically adjacent, no experiment run. Not to be confused with the causal-localization TADA! paper (2602.11910) featured heavily above, which is a separate paper with substantial real engagement.

entries.title: Bjerva 2017 (ACL W17-0225), information-theoretic prediction of MTL auxiliary-task benefit
entries.claim: Information-theoretic measures can predict whether an auxiliary task will help or hurt in multi-task learning (representation-sharing MTL, no frozen probe). Purely a conceptual cousin/citation ("cousin of the helps-half"), not tested against SAO's own data.
